description.narrative:
The programme aligns to the Global Strategic Framework as follows:
Enhanced humanitarian action
1. Humanitarian needs are addressed by life-saving assistance, ensuring rights of people are protected. 2. People, communities and duty bearers use their agency and capacities to lead, influence and hold the humanitarian system accountable as local humanitarian leaders. 3. Women and girls are adequately supported to participate and lead meaningfully in humanitarian action. 4. Humanitarian system is reoriented towards local leadership.
Accountable Governance
1. Robust governance frameworks provide safe spaces for people to hold duty bearers to account. 2. Feminist and youth movements are adequately supported and resourced.
Climate Justice
1. Local expertise and women’s leadership is resourced to build resilience and shape solutions. 2. People forced to migrate by the climate crisis find support in establishingnew lives and livelihoods.
Oxfam in SAF would like to align humanitarian action to be Rights, Resilience and Response Horizon Planthrough transforming the dynamic that produce and perpetuate fragility and inequality The Humanitarian Action seeks to strengthen capacities of local actors and communities at risk of conflict and climatic shocks to identify and prepare for hazards/disasters, have the ability to respond to disasters and recover from shocks and promote resilience. Oxfam in SAF would like to support partners and communities to address their immediate needs, upholds their rights and mobilize resources needed for immediate and long- term change Oxfam would continue to invest in mitigating risks through structured context, gender and power analysis in humanitarian action Program integration will be a key strategy to promote the humanitarian, Developmemt and peace nexus Oxfam will engage with donors and affiliates to mobilize flexible funds in support of local humanitarian action Oxfam will encourage the participation of local actors in strategic, national and regional coordination platforms for humanitarian action
The Humanitarian program goal is that: To strengthen capacities of people and communities at risk of conflict to prepare before hazards/disasters, ability to respond during disasters and enhance ability to recover after crises working together with partners and Oxfam.
Specific Objective 1: Disaster affectedpeople (men, women, boys and girls) receive timely and appropriate lifesaving assistance for Food, Water, Sanitation, Hygiene, Protection, Safeguarding and Gender.
-Improved access to safe, adequate and dignified water, sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion activities for vulnerable women, men, girls and boys. -Improved access to safe, and adequate and dignified access to food and income for vulnerable women, men, girls and boys. -The safety of women, girls, men and boys from the crisis-affected communities is enhanced through strengthened self-protection capacities. -Diversified income generation activities for households affected or prone to disaster prone areas. Provision of timely multipurpose cash/in-kind food assistance to people affected by natural disasters, conflict during and after the crisis period Develop and integrate low-cost innovations that offer sustainable and community driven solutions e.g. construction of solar Piped waters schemes eveloping Water and Sanitation age friendly facility (Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe) Establishing sustainable governance of water resources at local <(>&<)> national levels across the 4 countries Influencing people-centered health promotion interventions across the four countries Participating in Government and community-based budget consultation for WASH services Conduct food security and vulnerability assessments. Strategic Objective 2: Communities (men and women) impacted by conflict and recurring crises are supported to develop capacity to strengthen their resilience by 2025 Increased capacity of communities to plan, prepare and respond to disasters Strategic. Establishing community early warning systems, contingency planning, crisis modification Work with Governments line Ministries/Departments to develop District/Village Disaster Management andClimate Adaptation Plans and Response Plans. Hazard mapping and Prioritizing Hazards. Synergies Program integration- Just Economies and Gender Justice Capacity Building in DRR and Action Areas Multi sector coordination Develop/review district and local level early warning and disaster preparedness plans. Strategic Objective 3: Local humanitarian actors by gender are supported to lead humanitarian action in Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe by 2025 Increased capacity of local partners to anticipate, respond, mitigate disasters in their areas within SAF region. Continuous Partner mapping in SAF. Capacity development planning Networking with affiliates, regions and agencies for financing and capacity buildings Monitoring of safeguarding implementation, compliance Awareness andsafeguarding communication (translations IEC,) work to transform and decolonize the humanitarian system, reorienting towards local leadership ensuring aid is more effective, appropriate and tailored to meet local needs and expectations. promote the important roleof local and national actors and celebrate the work that they do. Ensure our engagements with communities and those who support them are based on the principles of inclusivity, equality and transparency. Involve Local and National Humanitarian Actors in the design of programmes at the outset and participate in decision-making as equals in influencing programme design and partnership policies. Expand opportunities for those impacted by crises to lead on developing sustainable solutions, supporting their participation in decision-making and coordination spaces. Increase funding to national and local NGOs for humanitarian action by at least 25% of our own humanitarian funding. Strategic Objective 4: Strengthened coordination and collaboration with multi-level, multisectoral and transboundary stakeholders towards rights, resilience and response by 2025 Improved in service delivery to disaster affected households by their governments in SAF. Increase in development and implementation of local <(>&<)> National risk reduction strategies in SAF. Research and Evidence building Develop a Humanitarian Influencing strategy Facilitate forums for discussions on humanitarian governance and influencing Capacity building local partners Strengthen partners capacity on advocacy for WASH Influence governments to deliver WASH <(>&<)> EFSEI services

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
